issues.problem: The docs describe Counter as a value that increases over time, but they do not state this as a runtime guarantee (Add does not reject negative values). The generator notes admit this was not checked. Stating it as a fact is slightly stronger than the source supports. The same wording appears in the RU explanation.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to: `Counter<T>` is meant for non-negative increments of a value that only grows. Apply the same change to the RU explanation: "`Counter<T>` рассчитан на неотрицательные приращения и подходит для растущих итогов".

issues.claim: When the state is a dictionary (any collection of `KeyValuePair<string, object>`), structured sinks get `OrderId` as a separate property you can filter on.
issues.problem: The built-in simple console formatter prints `scope.ToString()`, so with IncludeScopes enabled a `Dictionary<string, object>` appears as its type name, not as OrderId=... Only the JSON console formatter and structured providers such as Application Insights or OpenTelemetry expand the key-value pairs. A candidate may wrongly expect to see OrderId in the default console output. The RU text has the same gap.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a sentence to both explanations. EN: "The simple console formatter prints the scope via ToString(), so a dictionary shows up as its type name; use the JSON formatter or a structured provider to see OrderId as a property." RU: "Простой консольный форматировщик выводит область через ToString(), поэтому словарь печатается как имя типа; чтобы увидеть OrderId отдельным свойством, используйте JSON-форматировщик или структурированный провайдер."
